title: Shelving unfinished work
summary: git stash: switch branches without committing half-done work.

say.never: Imagine you're halfway through something that isn't ready to save, and a teammate asks you to fix a small bug on another branch *right now*. Git won't let you switch branches if it would overwrite your unfinished work. A **stash** is a shelf: put your unfinished work on it, switch and fix the bug, come back, and take your work off the shelf.
say.bit: Stash shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches (git refuses to switch when your changes would be overwritten), then `stash pop` restores them.

say.never: Open **Source Control** (the branch icon on the left). Each exercise folder has its own section there. Click **08-stash** so the buttons and menus work on that folder.
say.bit: In Source Control, click **08-stash** so the buttons act on it.

say.never: Click the branch name in the bottom-left and pick `develop`. Git refuses and says your local changes would be overwritten. That's exactly the problem a stash solves. Close the message and carry on.
say.bit: Try switching to `develop` from the branch name (bottom-left). Git refuses: your changes would be overwritten.

say.never: In Source Control, open **...**, then **Stash**, then **Stash**: your changes go on the shelf. Now switch to `develop`. Switch back to `issue-21-new-motor`, then open **...**, **Stash**, **Pop Latest Stash** to take your work off the shelf.
